note: ACC-501 seed run against the UNCORRECTED miner: significantEdges() gates on fixed thresholds (minLift 2, minZ 2, minSupport 3) with no multiple-comparisons correction and no de-clustering, so 22 of 256 mined edges clear and only 5 are real — coupling precision 22.7%. Recall is 1.0 and the engine's built-in rules are perfect on event-level truth (precision 1.0, recall 1.0, zero decoy leakage), so every unit of headroom here is in the miner, not the rules. The 14 unplanted edges split into two kinds: 6 are a systematic near-coincidence (the S2 grid-storm anchors sit a fixed ~0.5d before the S8 chain triplets, so space/infra -> chain-x/y/z score z=4.63 and will SURVIVE a Bonferroni correction), and 8 are weak incidental noise (z 2.5-4.8) that a correction should kill. Two real couplings (macro->maritime, space->infra) were evicted at MAX_LEARNED_RULES by burst artefacts, which is what edgeStrengthSeparation=0.05 measures: `strength` saturates at 1.0, so the ranking that decides the cap is nearly flat. It adds learnedPairs rows, a re-derived causal-rule roster, per-rule probes with one-clause near-misses, ruleCoverage, a confidence saturation/degeneracy guard, per-category false-positive growth gates, and miner-window validation. schemaVersion 8 answers a tenth round that pointed at the last circular seam: every check ran inside the process that produced the report, against truth from the same commit, so a change INSIDE runCorrelationBenchmark() moved the report and the comparator's re-run identically — deranged pair attribution, collapsed learned-pair rows, forged probe text and a deleted metric all passed, because none of them move an aggregate the committed file pins. ledgerDigest is the anchor that lives outside the process: a 128-bit digest of the edge, pair, learned-pair and probe rows, written into this file by the human who re-seeded it. A real miner change now fails on identity and must be re-seeded in a reviewed diff, which is the intended cost. It also makes edgeEvidenceSeparation nullable on the committed side (a perfect miner reports no false edges, and requiring a number here made the goal state un-seedable) and hardens the reproduction walk to own, plain-object keys (Object.create(realReport) had no own keys, serialized as {}, and reproduced). schemaVersion 9 answers an eleventh round that showed schemaVersion 8 pinned the wrong half of the report: ledgerDigest covered the row-level ledgers, so a producer-side change could still DELETE meanCausalEdgeStrength or meanCausalEdgeZ, or forge causalCouplingsLostToCap, meanFalsePairConfidence or confidenceSeparation, and return a clean PASS — the summary layer where the advertised measurements live was pinned by nothing but re-derivation inside the process that produced it. reportDigest replaces it and covers EVERY field, containers included (an array emits its length and an object its sorted key list before their contents, so a deleted field is not merely fewer records). Number quantization moved from 4 decimals to 9: at 4 a uniform strength-0.00001 applied across the whole producer reproduced the digest exactly, and 9 still sits five orders of magnitude above the libm last-bit noise that made rounding necessary in the first place. The reproduction walk now reads each field ONCE from its own property descriptor (Reflect.ownKeys, data descriptors only, enumerable only): an enumerable getter had been returning the real value to the comparator and a different value to the next consumer, and an extra non-enumerable own property was invisible to Object.keys and to JSON.stringify but not to a plain read. A baseline seeded from a perfect run (null separation, zero false edges) now forces falseEdgeGrowth to 0 rather than inheriting the tolerance, which is what the separation-exemption comment had always claimed. The cost of pinning the whole report is that an IMPROVEMENT also fails, on identity — `npm run bench:correlation -- --seed` prints the block to commit, and that re-seed diff is where a human reads the new numbers. schemaVersion 10 answers a twelfth round that found two things reportDigest could not see, because the report never carried them. Rule probes reported two booleans and a sentence about a fixture the report did not contain: re-aiming a near-miss at a clause the rule still has — moving n1b off GDACS while deleting the earthquake-tsunami distance check — left the positive matching, the near-miss rejecting on the source gate instead of the radius, and every leaf of the report identical. Each probe now carries a fixtureDigest over both fixtures' full event fields and the expected outcomes, so what was ASKED is pinned alongside the answer. And the pair ledger erased the two things the engine actually asserts about a pair before hashing: rewriting a rule from causal-candidate cause->effect to contradicts effect->cause was byte-identical in the report, while production maps both the edge type and the endpoint order into the evidence graph. Emissions are now rows of their own — ruleId, edgeType, and directed fromId/toId — and the unordered key stays the grading key, because planted truth is a claim about two events being related, not about which came first. This file also gained a witnessed block: the advertised-but-ungated measurements (meanCausalEdgeStrength, meanCausalEdgeZ, meanFalsePairConfidence, confidenceSeparation, causalCouplingsLostToCap) plus one digest per ledger, pinned by value. reportDigest already covered all of it; what it did not do is SHOW it, so the re-seed diff the digest prescribes reading was a single opaque 32-character string. No graded number moved in this re-seed — every metric above is identical to schemaVersion 9's.
